scheduleMemo: Fourteen Week 7 games, from Thursday night in Chicago to Monday night in Philadelphia. All kickoff times are Pacific.
openingMemo: New England gets my first look tonight. Graham has Chicago by one; the saved morning benchmark has Chicago by three. That puts two points on the Patriots’ side of the comparison, with enough unfinished personnel business to keep the final inactive list important.

Denver is the largest disagreement on the rest of the sheet. Las Vegas and Philadelphia also deserve time because Graham and the benchmark disagree on the favourite. Baltimore belongs in that conversation once its quarterback is settled. All fourteen games are below.
performanceMemo: Two wins and twelve losses is a poor Week 6. The season comparison is now 45–44–4, or 50.6% against the saved Pinnacle spreads. That record stays at the front of this sheet.
Those same fourteen games gave the favourites six wins and the underdogs eight. The season underdog comparison is 49–40–4, ahead of Graham. I’m keeping it beside his record.
Pinnacle’s saved numbers also remain closer to the final margins overall. I still want to examine a meaningful disagreement, and I want a football reason that stands up to the personnel news.
changeMemo: This Week 7 Thursday edition replaces the October 6 Week 5 guest copy. The earlier sheet remains in the archive. All fourteen current-week games are covered, and the performance record now includes every final through Week 6.

Graham’s prior-week learning and Week 7 baseline are complete. Baltimore and Tampa Bay still have unresolved quarterback decisions, and every matchup has open personnel questions. The Giants’ quarterback decision is settled with J.J. McCarthy; I have removed that old question from their file.
The number panels retain this morning’s saved Pinnacle observations. They are dated comparisons. Tonight’s final inactives arrive after this edition’s review and still need checking before kickoff.

reviews.read: New England is my first file tonight: Chicago by one on Graham’s sheet against Chicago by three on the morning benchmark. The quarterbacks are settled. Morgan Moses, New England’s remaining line assignments, and Chicago’s Edwards and Stevenson questions still matter; eleven personnel cases remain open in total. Carlton Davis and Kyle Monangai are already included in the number. I want the final inactive list before strengthening the Patriots’ case.
reviews.note: Patriots get the comparison. Check the line and the final inactives before kickoff.

reviews.read: New Orleans has a modest point in hand: Pittsburgh by two and a half on Graham’s sheet against three and a half on the benchmark. Kamara, Ruiz and the Saints’ defensive personnel questions deserve more attention than dressing up that one point. This is the early Sunday file, with a 6:30 a.m. Pacific kickoff.
reviews.note: Saints get a second look. Have the personnel answers before the early start.

reviews.read: San Francisco is the side I want to examine at the saved three. Graham makes five and a half, leaving a two-and-a-half-point disagreement. Bosa, Samuel, Evans and several secondary questions are still open, while Atlanta has Deablo and Bowman among its unresolved cases. Fourteen unfinished personnel items make the health picture central to this read.
reviews.note: 49ers stay on the watchlist. The personnel answers have to support the gap.

reviews.read: Baltimore is the favourite on Graham’s sheet by three and a half; the saved benchmark makes Cincinnati the one-point favourite. That is four and a half points toward the Ravens, and the quarterback decision is still outstanding. I am holding the stronger opinion until Baltimore names its starter. Jurgens, Pocic, Bateman and Stanley add further questions.
reviews.note: Ravens go back to the top of the file when the starter is confirmed.

reviews.read: Carolina’s five against the benchmark three is a two-point comparison toward the Panthers. Tampa Bay’s quarterback decision is still open, with a low-confidence prior estimate retained in the number. Mayfield’s full practice is encouraging; it does not settle Sunday’s starter. I want that answer before giving Carolina more weight.
reviews.note: Panthers have the numerical case. Tampa Bay’s quarterback answer comes first.

reviews.read: The Giants have two points in the comparison: Houston by eight and a half on Graham’s sheet against ten and a half on the benchmark. McCarthy is already confirmed as New York’s starter, so that question is closed. Burns, Thomas, Eluemunor and Tracy remain among the open Giants cases, with Houston’s Smith, Montgomery and Pitre also unresolved. I want those answers before leaning harder on the extra room.
reviews.note: Giants are worth the review. Keep the resolved quarterback separate from the open injuries.

reviews.read: Minnesota’s seven and a half against the saved six and a half is a quiet point toward the Vikings. Warren and Dulin remain open for Indianapolis; Darrisaw, Addison, Mason and Hockenson remain open for Minnesota. I am keeping this below the larger disagreements until that group clears.
reviews.note: One point toward Minnesota. Keep the size of the opinion in proportion.

reviews.read: The Jets get a point and a half in the comparison, six on Graham’s sheet against four and a half on the benchmark. Achane’s estimated absence effect is already included for Miami. Hall, Mitchell, Parham and Ossai remain among the Jets’ open cases, so their answers matter to the same side the numbers favour.
reviews.note: Jets get another pass after the personnel check. Achane is already in the number.

reviews.read: Tennessee receives half a point in the comparison: Cleveland by one on Graham’s sheet against one and a half on the benchmark. There are six open personnel cases across the two clubs. Half a point keeps this near the bottom of my review order.
reviews.note: A small Tennessee difference. Leave room for the more useful files.

reviews.read: Denver is my first deep Sunday review. Graham makes eleven against the saved four, the largest gap on the page at seven points. Arizona’s existing personnel adjustments are already part of that number. Surtain and Hufanga for Denver, and Harrison, Love, Nolen and Sweat for Arizona, remain unresolved. I want to understand those answers before trusting a disagreement this large.
reviews.note: Denver heads the Sunday research list. Seven points deserve a proper explanation.

reviews.read: Both displayed columns make Detroit three. There is no number disagreement to promote. Green Bay still has Banks, St-Juste, Kraft, Lloyd and Cisse open, so I will follow those changes and leave this behind the games where the columns differ.
reviews.note: Detroit three in both columns. Revisit if the personnel picture changes.

reviews.read: Las Vegas is one of the more interesting Sunday files. Graham makes the Raiders one-and-a-half-point favourites while the benchmark makes the Rams four-point favourites, five and a half points toward Las Vegas. The Rams’ existing estimated losses are already doing work in that fair. McDuffie and Atwell remain open, and two Raiders valuation cases remain unfinished. I want those assumptions clear before treating the reversal as persuasive.
reviews.note: Raiders get a serious review. Keep the Rams’ already-applied losses in view.

reviews.read: Kansas City has one point in the comparison: Seattle by one and a half on Graham’s sheet against two and a half on the benchmark. Rice and Simmons remain open for Kansas City, with Drake Thomas still open for Seattle. This is a secondary Sunday-night file until those questions are answered.
reviews.note: Chiefs get the smaller comparison. Keep the Sunday-night updates in order.

reviews.read: Philadelphia is the Monday file I want to spend time on. Graham makes the Eagles one-point favourites; the benchmark makes Dallas four-and-a-half-point favourites. The five-and-a-half-point reversal comes with seventeen open personnel cases and a low-confidence Philadelphia quarterback prior. Barkley, Dickerson, Turpin and Durant are among the names still needing answers. There is time to make this a better-informed opinion before Monday.
reviews.note: Eagles stay high on the Monday watchlist. Leave the final judgment open for the personnel news.

closingWatchlist: Tonight: New England gets my attention first, with two points in the saved comparison. The final inactive list and New England’s line assignments are the next checks. Chicago remains Graham’s one-point favourite.

Sunday: Denver heads the deeper review, followed by Las Vegas and San Francisco. The Giants belong in the next group. Baltimore’s larger reversal stays conditional on its starter, and Tampa Bay’s decision still shapes the Carolina file.
Monday: Philadelphia gets a proper second reading when its personnel picture is clearer. All fourteen games remain on this sheet. No order.
signature: Keep the record in front of us. Make the next game earn its place. — Bill
